policy: Each note states observed read depth: catalogued, abstract-reviewed, partially-studied (specified original pages), or fully-studied (only after comprehensive critical review). Never count abstracts or targeted pages as fully studied. Source-level verdict reasons are audited separately.

notes.label: Hawking: chronology protection
notes.summary: Hawking analyzes whether compactly generated chronology horizons can appear without pathologies, arguing the quantum stress-energy response may obstruct their formation.
notes.limitations: This is a conjecture supported by analysis under assumptions; it is not a general proof forbidding all conceivable backwards travel.
notes.conclusion: Physics of chronology protection is undecided; does not imply either one or multiple branches.
notes.confidence: Bounded to publisher/archival summary; not a full-text critical review

notes.label: Bothwell et al.: redshift at millimetre scales
notes.summary: An optical atomic clock can resolve differences in gravitational redshift across a millimetre-scale sample, a precise test of the Einsteinian prediction.
notes.limitations: Clock comparison concerns relative ticking at different potentials. It is not a trajectory into the past and does not discriminate Everett interpretations.
notes.conclusion: Strengthens established relativistic time dilation only.
notes.confidence: Bounded to publisher/archival summary; not a full-text critical review

notes.label: Everett: relative state
notes.summary: Everett's work proposes the relative-state formulation of quantum mechanics, important to no-collapse approaches.
notes.limitations: The interpretive account requires connecting universal quantum evolution to experiences; existence of the formulation is not laboratory proof of splitting.
notes.conclusion: Important theoretical hypothesis, zero empirical branch-count credit.
notes.confidence: Bounded to publisher/archival summary; not a full-text critical review

notes.label: Bell: locality
notes.summary: Bell's theorem establishes testable constraints on a class of local hidden-variable accounts.
notes.limitations: Violations challenge locality assumptions, not automatically single-history interpretations; competing nonlocal or no-collapse theories differ.
notes.conclusion: Crucial falsifiability template, not a direct one-world/many-world test.
notes.confidence: Bounded to publisher/archival summary; not a full-text critical review

notes.label: Zurek: decoherence
notes.summary: Interactions with the environment suppress interference and favor dynamically robust pointer states, helping explain apparently classical records.
notes.limitations: Decoherence by itself does not uniquely decide whether collapse, hidden variables or many-worlds ontology is correct.
notes.conclusion: Mechanistic explanation reviewed; no direct compass change.
notes.confidence: Bounded to publisher/archival summary; not a full-text critical review

notes.label: Deutsch: closed timelike quantum lines
notes.summary: Deutsch applies quantum-computation methods to systems interacting with hypothetical closed timelike lines, describing nonclassical consistency behavior.
notes.limitations: The exotic spacetime is assumed in the model; it has not been demonstrated as a travel-accessible physical apparatus.
notes.conclusion: Mathematical model indexed, no observed timeline crossings.
notes.confidence: Bounded to publisher/archival summary; not a full-text critical review

notes.label: Oreshkov et al.: causal order
notes.summary: A framework allows quantum correlations without preassigned global causal order, highlighting formal alternatives to classical process ordering.
notes.limitations: Indefinite causal order should not be conflated with an observer returning to a prior macroscopic history.
notes.conclusion: New formal questions, not direct multiple-history measurement.
notes.confidence: Bounded to publisher/archival summary; not a full-text critical review

notes.label: Eagleman: experienced time
notes.summary: Human experience of duration and temporal order is susceptible to measurable distortions and illusions.
notes.limitations: Perceptual anomalies and misordered subjective events do not modify causal spacetime or establish an alternate chronology.
notes.conclusion: Useful category guardrail for neuroscience, neutral to physical branch count.
notes.confidence: Bounded to publisher/archival summary; not a full-text critical review

notes.label: Hornberger et al.: molecular interference
notes.summary: Interference of relatively complex molecules offers controlled tests of quantum superposition and environmental decoherence.
notes.limitations: Molecular interference supports quantum behavior, not a unique ontology of observed macroscopic branches.
notes.conclusion: High research priority for tests of collapse alternatives, still nondiscriminating here.
notes.confidence: Bounded to publisher/archival summary; not a full-text critical review

notes.label: Nobel scientific background: biological clocks
notes.summary: Circadian rhythms arise from endogenous genetic and biochemical feedback loops, as documented in Nobel historical material.
notes.limitations: The circadian oscillator tracks and anticipates local day/night cycles, but its biology cannot establish spacetime topology.
notes.conclusion: Biological-clock measurements are separate from relativistic clocks.
notes.confidence: Bounded to publisher/archival summary; not a full-text critical review

notes.label: Wormhole chronology versus actual spacetime engineering
notes.summary: Morris, Thorne and Yurtsever describe a conditional route from a traversable wormhole to a time machine, assuming such a wormhole can be constructed and maintained.
notes.limitations: The abstract itself flags weak-energy and quantum-gravity uncertainties. It does not report the creation of a traversable wormhole or demonstrate backward time travel.
notes.conclusion: Adds a conditional theoretical challenge to the research syllabus, but no empirical discrimination of physical histories.
notes.confidence: Scoped to accessible abstract; no full text or independent replication review

notes.label: GRW objective-collapse dynamics
notes.basis: American Physical Society journal abstract · https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.34.470
notes.summary: Ghirardi, Rimini and Weber propose a modified dynamical model that aims to recover microscopic quantum behavior and classical localization for macroscopic systems.
notes.limitations: A formulated alternative is not by itself experimental confirmation; the relevant tests require precise collapse parameters and constraints.
notes.conclusion: Provides a serious competing mechanism for measurement outcomes without proving or refuting Everett branches.
notes.confidence: Scoped to accessible abstract; no full text or independent replication review

notes.label: Extended Wigner-friend experimental assumptions
notes.basis: Science Advances / PubMed research abstract · https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.aaw9832
notes.summary: Proietti and collaborators describe a six-photon extended Wigner-friend experiment and a Bell-type inequality violation tied to observer-independent-facts assumptions.
notes.limitations: The inference is conditional on assumptions including locality and free choice, and does not amount to an experimental observation of travel or interaction between alternate histories.
notes.conclusion: Observer-independent descriptions face nontrivial assumptions; no physically realized branching census is established.
notes.confidence: Scoped to accessible abstract; no full text or independent replication review

notes.label: Large-molecule quantum interference constraints
notes.summary: Fein and colleagues report matter-wave interference involving molecules exceeding 25 kDa and discuss tests that constrain modifications to quantum mechanics.
notes.limitations: Molecular interferometry is not an observation of multiple universes; experimental methods and collapse-model bounds need detailed full-text examination.
notes.conclusion: Raises priority for the chemistry and quantum-foundations cross-lab without shifting the history-count verdict.
notes.confidence: Scoped to accessible abstract; no full text or independent replication review

notes.label: Gödel original rotating spacetime and timelike circle
notes.basis: Original published PDF https://journals.aps.org/rmp/pdf/10.1103/RevModPhys.21.447 ; examined pp. 447 (main properties and metric), 448 (field equation setting), 449 (section 3 timelike circular orbit).
sectionsRead: §3 p.449 (construction of circular timelike line)
notes.summary: Exact rotating homogeneous cosmological solution can be time-oriented without a global monotonically increasing time coordinate; sufficiently large circular timelike lines are closed. Mathematical permission is shown for this geometry, not an empirical demonstration of actual loops.
notes.method: Direct original text review of model assumptions, properties (4)-(6), field-equation context and construction at p.449.
notes.limitations: Not a replication of all tensor algebra or complete review of §4. No evidence this spacetime is an observed cosmological model.
notes.alternativeExplanations: Physical chronology protection may prevent formation from realistic initially causal conditions; CTCs are not equivalent to Everett branch multiplicity.
notes.conclusion: Strong mathematical-existence result with zero direct evidential support for count or accessibility of alternate physical histories.

notes.label: Hawking original chronology-horizon restrictions
notes.basis: Original paper PDF hosted by CfA https://lweb.cfa.harvard.edu/~loeb/Hawking_C.pdf ; examined p.603 §I, pp.604-606 selected §II, p.606 §III, pp.608-609 selected §IV, p.610 §VI.
sectionsRead: §II pp.604-606 (selected)
§III p.606 (selected)
§IV pp.608-609 (selected)
notes.summary: Compactly generated horizon assumptions imply constraints under energy conditions, while semiclassical stress-energy/backreaction may inhibit formation of CTCs; quantum gravity caveats remain.
notes.method: Check claims against primary paper introduction, geometric argument for compact horizon, semiclassical section and conclusion.
notes.limitations: Some intermediate proofs and renormalized-field steps not reproduced. Hawking's conjecture is not an experimental theorem or universal prohibition of every eternal CTC geometry.
notes.alternativeExplanations: Exceptional horizon settings, exotic matter, quantum gravity cutoffs and untested alternative gravitational dynamics must be considered.
notes.conclusion: Conditional theoretical reason to doubt engineering chronology violation, no measurement of branches and no reason to shift the compass.

notes.label: Deutsch 1991 density-matrix fixed-point calculation
notes.basis: Published paper accessible scan https://gwern.net/doc/science/physics/1991-deutsch.pdf ; examined pp.3197-3199, 3202-3204; especially eqs.15-18 p.3203 and maximum entropy choice p.3204.
sectionsRead: Introduction pp.3197-3199
Quantum computational analysis pp.3202-3203
Fixed point proof eqs.15-18 p.3203
Maximum entropy rule p.3204
notes.summary: A prescribed CTC finite-state quantum network admits density operator fixed points; averaged channel iterates and compactness support existence. Some cases allow multiple states and invoke an extra maximum-entropy selection postulate.
notes.method: Original-paper check of consistency equation, quantum channel averaging construction and alternative fixed-point-selection issue.
notes.limitations: Geometry and path are assumed, not physically created; the rest of paper's examples and later interpretive analysis require full reading.
notes.alternativeExplanations: Politzer path-integral analysis and Lloyd postselected-teleportation theory yield inequivalent hypothetical CTC dynamics; no direct observation breaks this tie.
notes.conclusion: A significant conditional consistency model, not empirical access to quantum alternate histories.

notes.label: Politzer countermodel of CTC information flow
notes.summary: Different closed-timelike-curve quantum prescriptions can be inequivalent and can handle coherence, unitarity and information differently.
notes.limitations: Publisher abstract only; full derivations and sample system have not been examined.
notes.conclusion: Challenges uniqueness of Deutsch conditional modeling, supplies no realized CTC or branch-count observation.

notes.label: Lloyd et al. postselected-teleportation alternative
notes.basis: APS publisher abstract https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.84.025007 and MIT repository metadata https://dspace.mit.edu/entities/publication/4e961ae6-417d-4811-81ea-7aa85bcc055f
notes.summary: P-CTC approach based on postselected teleportation is inequivalent to Deutsch's model and uses a different self-consistency construction.
notes.limitations: Abstract-level reading; no detailed validation of simulation circuit, postselection probability or path integrals.
notes.conclusion: Illustrates model-dependence of hypothetical loop dynamics, not physical time-loop proof.

notes.label: Independent sign check of Gödel circular timelike path
notes.basis: Gödel original §3 p.449 https://journals.aps.org/rmp/pdf/10.1103/RevModPhys.21.447; hand algebra and numeric evaluation of the published metric's constant-r circle coefficient.
notes.summary: Setting dt=dr=dy=0 in transformed metric gives g_phi_phi=4a²sinh²r(sinh²r−1), timelike for r>asinh(1)=ln(1+sqrt(2))≈0.881373587; sign checks at r=0.5 and 1.0 agree.
notes.method: Symbolic factorization and numerical values: inner coefficient at r=0.5 −0.1978061734 and r=1.0 +0.5263334134.
notes.limitations: Local metric sign check does not validate Einstein-equation solution independently or demonstrate an observable physical CTC.
notes.alternativeExplanations: Real-world spacetime need not possess Gödel's global rotating cosmological geometry.
notes.conclusion: A partial mathematical derivation replicated, with no additional physical-history evidence.

notes.label: One-bit Deutsch consistency toy computed
notes.basis: Deutsch original discussion of paradoxes and eqs.15-18 pp.3202-3203; maximum-entropy postulate p.3204, accessible https://gwern.net/doc/science/physics/1991-deutsch.pdf.
sectionsRead: pp.3202-3204, especially eqs.15-18 and maximum entropy rule
notes.summary: Classical deterministic NOT map lacks a Boolean fixed point. Quantum channel Phi(rho)=XrhoX fixes both I/2 and the pure plus state; max-entropy selection chooses I/2 among these.
notes.method: Exact matrix multiplication and eigenvalue calculation for a 2x2 X gate with I/2 and |+><+|; residual zero for both.
notes.limitations: Assumes a loop/self-consistency constraint rather than observing one; does not reproduce Deutsch's complete network or nonlinear effective CR dynamics.
notes.alternativeExplanations: Other CTC consistency models may predict inequivalent dynamics; ordinary laboratory gates cannot demonstrate physical chronology violation.
notes.conclusion: Conditional model statement reproduced as a toy calculation; no empirical branch detection.

notes.label: Hawking formation argument: precise assumptions and semiclassical exception
notes.basis: Original PRD 46 (1992) PDF https://lweb.cfa.harvard.edu/~loeb/Hawking_C.pdf, §II pp.604–606, §III pp.606–607, §IV p.608–609, §VI pp.610–611.
sectionsRead: §II pp.604–606 compact generation from a bounded local region
§III pp.606–607 noncompact initial surface and weak-energy condition
§IV pp.608–609 Misner-space free-field illustration
§VI pp.610–611 exceptions and heuristic backreaction
notes.summary: The local-manufacture argument is framed around compactly generated future Cauchy horizons. With a noncompact initial surface a weak-energy-condition obstruction occurs; Hawking then argues, using semiclassical fields and example geometries, that large vacuum polarization/backreaction may prevent chronology formation. The conclusion remains a conjecture rather than a proof for arbitrary quantum gravity.
notes.method: Revisited original section statements, distinguished geometric energy-condition inference from model-specific quantum stress growth and hypothetical backreaction.
notes.limitations: No independent reproduction of full Raychaudhuri/Newman–Penrose integrations or stress-tensor renormalization; the excerpted model arguments do not decide all interacting fields and geometries.
notes.alternativeExplanations: Kay–Radzikowski–Wald prove a different local QFT breakdown theorem; Visser argues semiclassical gravity can lose reliability before its backreaction is predictive.
notes.conclusion: Strong but assumption-dependent theoretical case. Does not establish that quantum gravity universally forbids all CTCs or the count of physical histories.

notes.label: Kay–Radzikowski–Wald: theorem is singular or ill-defined Hadamard behavior, not universal metric blowup
notes.basis: Original arXiv gr-qc/9603012v2 https://arxiv.org/pdf/gr-qc/9603012, introduction PDF pp.1–5, §4 pp.24–25 (F-locality), §5 pp.27–28 (Theorem 2 and proof), §6 p.30 (comparison and limitations).
sectionsRead: Abstract PDF pp.1–2
Introduction PDF pp.2–5
§4 F-locality candidate PDF pp.24–25
§5 Theorem 2/proof PDF pp.27–28
§6 physical interpretation PDF p.30
notes.summary: For a linear Klein–Gordon quantum field on a spacetime with compactly generated Cauchy horizon, base points obstruct F-local field-algebra extension and universally regular Hadamard two-point extension; a mismatch fails even local L² regularity, leaving renormalized quantities undefined or singular there. This is stronger than generic expectation of stress divergence but narrower than proving time machines cannot form.
notes.method: Checked original theorem statements, geometric assumptions, proof's null-geodesic/local-vs-global singularity comparison, and authors' explicit interpretation caveats; did not reproduce microlocal propagation-of-singularities theorem.
notes.limitations: Original proof relies on distributional and microlocal results not independently verified here; theorem's domain is compactly generated horizon, prescribed linear field, and base points. No universal matter+quantum-gravity evolution result.
notes.alternativeExplanations: Some states can show bounded stress on approach yet fail Hadamard condition at base points; quantum gravity could change the framework.
notes.conclusion: Conditional rigorous obstruction to standard QFT at specified horizon points; not experimental demonstration of chronology protection or multiple histories.

notes.label: Visser: reliability horizon versus chronology horizon
notes.basis: Original arXiv gr-qc/9702041v2 https://arxiv.org/pdf/gr-qc/9702041, §I–III pp.1–2, §IV pp.2–4, §V p.4; publisher metadata DOI 10.1016/S0370-2693(97)01226-4.
sectionsRead: §I PDF p.1
§II PDF pp.1–2
§III PDF p.2
§IV PDF pp.2–4 selected definitions
§V PDF p.4
notes.summary: Defines an invariantly motivated unreliable region using short nontrivial spacelike geodesics, Planck-scale curvature and a reliability horizon. Argues metric fluctuations can invalidate semiclassical gravitational prediction even when expected stress/backreaction remains small before a chronology horizon.
notes.method: Direct study of original definitions (including winding/curvature extensions), section III treatment of KRW, and section V conclusions; compared to Hawking's expectation-based backreaction argument.
notes.limitations: The reliability threshold and interpretation assume extrapolation of semiclassical effective gravity to short closed paths; it is not a full quantum-gravity solution. The full text and all steps have not been independently reconstructed.
notes.alternativeExplanations: Chronology protection might still be enforced by full quantum gravity or pre-horizon effects in specific geometries; an unreliable approximation is not permission for physical CTCs.
notes.conclusion: Highlights a central limit of semiclassical predictions without establishing an experimentally realized loop.

notes.label: Visser Roman ring: example of conditional weak backreaction
notes.basis: APS publisher abstract https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.55.5212 (no full paper review).
notes.summary: A postulated ring of traversable wormholes can be arranged in a model to keep vacuum polarization small up to a semiclassical reliability horizon, challenging a universal inference from large mean stress.
notes.limitations: Publisher abstract only; no independent derivation, constructed wormholes, or observed chronology violations.
notes.alternativeExplanations: Quantum metric fluctuations, energy inequalities and gravitational consistency may still forbid physical construction.
notes.conclusion: Conditional counterexample to a universal *mean-backreaction argument*, not evidence of a working time machine.

notes.label: Everett relative-state branch ontology
notes.basis: SEP revised June 2026 §§1,2.1,6; Everett 1957 publisher journal page
notes.summary: In Everett one evolving universal quantum state may contain many branch-relative macroscopic histories, but branch ontology is interpretive and no accessible direct branch census has been measured.
notes.limitations: Original Everett paper not fully read; preferred basis and Born weights require deeper criticism.
notes.alternativeExplanations: Multiple physical ontologies can yield indistinguishable current quantum statistics; avoid reading experiment as a branch census.
notes.conclusion: Central one-versus-many actual-history question not experimentally settled.

notes.label: Decoherence does not select one actual outcome

notes.basis: Pusey Barrett Rudolph 2012 Nature Physics publisher abstract

notes.label: Bell — On the Einstein Podolsky Rosen paradox (1964) — full critical review
sectionsRead: Complete original six-page paper, Physics 1, 195–200, §§I–VI including examples, quantitative contradiction, generalization and conclusion.
notes.summary: The singlet predicts E(a,b)=−a·b. A hidden-variable average of local preassigned A(a,λ), B(b,λ) with setting-independent response and a probability distribution for λ cannot reproduce all quantum spin correlations. Bell constructs one-spin hidden-variable and simpler correlation examples first to show why the locality condition—not the mere existence of hidden variables—drives the contradiction.
notes.method: Traced the normalization/perfect anticorrelation condition to Bell’s restriction on response functions, his inequality in §IV and the angle-smoothed non-approximation argument. Separately checked the related CHSH singlet configuration: four coplanar axes yield |S|=2√2≈2.828>2. This CHSH crosscheck is NOT a rederivation of Bell’s specific equation (22).
notes.limitations: Original theorem relies on locality and independence of measurement choices from λ, and on identifying outcomes/setting response appropriately; later experiments face statistical and detection assumptions. Bell does not forbid explicitly nonlocal Bohmian dynamics; the abstract claim that all hidden variables were ruled out is incorrect.
notes.alternativeExplanations: Bohm’s 1952 nonlocal theory, and the carefully different assumptions of 2015 loophole-free Bell tests; examine outcome independence, parameter independence and superdeterminism debates next.
notes.conclusion: Strong theorem against specified local hidden-variable accounts, ZERO direct proof that another physically real quantum history exists.
notes.readDepthDefinition: Entire main source read and critiqued; replication or external supplements not independently certified unless stated

notes.label: Pusey–Barrett–Rudolph — On the reality of the quantum state (2012) — full critical review
sectionsRead: Entire eight-page arXiv manuscript: definitions and toy example pp.1–2, n-system construction and noise bound pp.2–4, conclusion pp.4–5, Appendix A pp.5–6, Appendix B pp.7–8, Appendix C p.8.
notes.summary: Define an ontic microstate λ prepared according to μψ(λ); overlapping support for different pure quantum states encodes a ψ-epistemic picture. Assuming independent preparations produce independent physical states, n copies yield a nonzero chance of a common overlap for all 2^n preparation combinations. A joint exclusion measurement assigns a zero-probability outcome to each such combination, contradicting an overlap model.
notes.method: Directly checked the four two-qubit exclusion states of Eq.(1) against |00>, |0+>, |+0>, |++>: each forbidden inner product is numerically zero (residual <3×10^−17); the four measurement vectors are orthonormal (residual <5×10^−16). Examined Appendix A n-system circuit, Appendix B overlap/total-variation noise bound and Appendix C numerical semidefinite-program discussion; the general circuit and optimization were not independently reconstructed.
notes.limitations: Preparation independence and ontic-state sufficiency are substantive assumptions. Paper tests whether the wavefunction is 'mere information' about λ in a defined model family—not the existence or count of Everett branches. Cannot infer many worlds from ψ-ontology.
notes.alternativeExplanations: Preparation-correlated models, contextual responses, ontology distinctions in Bohmian and Everett interpretations; seek a recent critical reconstruction of theorem assumptions.
notes.conclusion: Rigorous, assumption-scoped constraint on ψ-epistemic models; zero direct history-multiplicity evidence.
notes.readDepthDefinition: Entire main source read and critiqued; replication or external supplements not independently certified unless stated

notes.label: Feeney et al. — First Observational Tests of Eternal Inflation (2011) — full critical review
sectionsRead: Complete five-page original paper: theory/templates, simulation/data selection, needlets and Hough edge detection, patch-wise Bayesian evidence, WMAP results and references.
notes.summary: Some eternal-inflation models produce observable bubble-collision perturbations with axial symmetry and a causal boundary, modeled by angular temperature profiles. Their pipeline tests for candidate patches and circular edges in foreground-masked WMAP W-band data, then assesses evidence ratios for collision templates vs ΛCDM.
notes.method: Checked 94-GHz W-band choice, 70.6% unmasked sky, noise/foreground simulation logic, needlet significance thresholds, edge detector and MultiNest patch-evidence prior choices. Paper reports 15 blobs minus four masked = 11 evaluated; strongest inference posterior peaks at zero mean detectable collisions, with mean number <1.6 at 68% credibility. The original analysis code/maps were not rerun.
notes.limitations: Bound is on detectable collision signals under assumed priors, template, masking and survey sensitivity, NOT on the total number of inaccessible bubble regions. An arXiv PDF may be later recompiled; 2011 publication and source model provenance are distinct. Inflation bubbles are ontologically different from Everett branches.
notes.alternativeExplanations: Foregrounds, four somewhat anomalous patches, later Planck-era data and alternate collision templates; require fresh full-survey reproduction to update cosmological verdict.
notes.conclusion: Model-conditional null CMB result; neither establishes nor eliminates a cosmological multiverse and cannot identify quantum branch count.
notes.readDepthDefinition: Entire main source read and critiqued; replication or external supplements not independently certified unless stated

notes.label: Vaidman — Many-Worlds Interpretation of Quantum Mechanics (SEP, revised 2026) — full critical review
sectionsRead: Full scholarly entry, revised 17 June 2026, §§1–8 including definitions, macroscopic state mapping, preferred basis, probability, nonlocality, tests, explicit objections, conclusion and bibliography overview.
notes.summary: MWI treats the universal quantum state as evolving without fundamental collapse, and defines experienced macroscopic worlds as approximate correlated components. It distinguishes the mathematical single global state from empirical experiences of many definite-looking worlds. It outlines Born-weight/post-measurement self-location, decoherence as preferred-basis motivation and disagreements over probability and explanatory adequacy.
notes.method: Read all eight sections, including the world's approximate/FAPP status, orthogonal decomposition ∑αᵢ|worldᵢ>, the Born-weight postulate, proposed macroscopic interference tests, criticisms and the author's reply. Critically separated authorial advocacy from uncontested physics and from direct experiments. Checked logical counterpoint that Bohmian mechanics may predict identical tested statistics with one actual configuration.
notes.limitations: Scholarly interpretive overview, not an experimental research paper and no direct measurement of branch ontology. World individuation and observer-weight probability are debated; the text itself notes realism tests against Bohm may be infeasible. Full bibliography was indexed as context, not every cited work separately studied.
notes.alternativeExplanations: Bohmian definite positions, GRW physical collapse and critiques by Kent, Albert and Hemmo/Shenker; full original studies remain valuable.
notes.conclusion: Full scholarly resource examined; establishes the structure and controversies of MWI, not empirical plurality of realized histories.
notes.readDepthDefinition: Entire main source read and critiqued; replication or external supplements not independently certified unless stated

notes.label: Oreshkov–Costa–Brukner — Quantum correlations with no causal order (2012) — full critical review
sectionsRead: Complete open-access journal main article: problem setup, causal inequality, quantum instruments and process matrices, nonseparable example, classical limit, discussion and methods (PMC main text). Supplementary derivations separately flagged not independently replicated.
notes.summary: In a binary communication task under a definite causal order and independently chosen bits, one direction cannot transmit information and success ≤3/4. If quantum operations remain valid *locally* but no global definite order is assumed, process matrices allow causally nonseparable correlations. Their explicit two-party process exceeds the causal inequality.
notes.method: Traced closed-lab/free-choice assumptions, CPTP/CJ machinery and normalization, and the example in their Eqs.(7)–(8). Checked the illustrative maximum (2+√2)/4≈0.853553 against 0.75, a gap of ≈0.10355. This numerical check is not a full independent proof of positivity of their process matrix or the supplementary classification.
notes.limitations: A mathematically permitted process with no presupposed global causal order is not an observed gravitational spacetime, and is not proof of physically branching outcomes. Supplementary formalization remains a specific unreplicated component.
notes.alternativeExplanations: Quantum-switch optical implementations have different operational assumptions from this causal-inequality model; avoid claiming those experiments directly test the Oreshkov inequality.
notes.conclusion: Formal expansion of admissible causal structures, neutral on one-versus-many actual quantum histories.
notes.readDepthDefinition: Entire main source read and critiqued; replication or external supplements not independently certified unless stated

notes.label: Procopio et al. — Experimental superposition of orders of quantum gates (2015) — full critical review
sectionsRead: Entire open-access journal main text, theory/commutation task, interferometer configuration, all Pauli-gate and 100 random-pair results, discussion and Methods subsections. Separate supplementary PDF identified, not independently reproduced.
notes.summary: A photon's path coherently controls the order of two polarization gates in a Mach–Zehnder-type interferometer. With the promise that gates commute or anticommute, measurement of the control can identify the relation with one use of each gate, surpassing the success ceiling for fixed-order protocols under the stated query model.
notes.method: Read gate-use operational definition, 16 Pauli combinations, 50 commuting and 50 anticommuting random cases, optical apparatus, results and noise controls. Reported random-pair correctness 0.976±0.015 vs fixed-order probabilistic bound 0.9288 and Pauli-case rate 0.973±0.016. Algebra sanity check: XZ=−ZX and IX=XI; interference control can encode the sign. Did not independently rerun photon counts or derive the supplementary quantum-comb optimum.
notes.limitations: Gate order in an interferometer is an operational quantum-circuit resource in one laboratory spacetime; not a human returning to another history or evidence of coexisting macroscopic worlds. Fixed-order comparison rests on carefully specified allowed queries and promises.
notes.alternativeExplanations: Later discussions distinguish causally nonseparable operations from indefinite metric or globally indefinite spacetime; preserve this boundary in lab visuals.
notes.conclusion: Strong quantum-information experiment, zero empirical branch-census impact.
